subject: Day 1: Here we go. Genesis.
body:
Good morning.

Today is the day. You signed up for this. I signed up for this. And right now, a group of us are opening to Genesis 1 together.

Yes, the whole book of Genesis today. Fifty chapters. I am not going to sugarcoat it. That is a lot. But here is what I want you to know. Genesis reads fast. It is all story. Creation, the flood, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Joseph. You will get pulled in.

Do not worry about understanding every detail. Do not stop to study. Just read. Let the words wash over you. You are not writing a paper. You are meeting God in His Word.

If you cannot finish all 50 chapters today, that is okay. Read what you can. Mark where you stopped. Come back to it. The goal is not perfection. The goal is showing up.

I am reading alongside you today.

Heather

subject: Day 2: Slavery, plagues, and a God who shows up
body:
Good morning.

Yesterday was Genesis. Today is Exodus. And the tone shifts fast.

The people of God go from favor to slavery in the first chapter. And then God raises up Moses, a man who did not want the job, to lead them out.

Here is what stood out to me when I read this. God did not wait for Moses to be ready. He did not wait for the people to have it together. He showed up because He heard them crying. That was enough.

Today you will read about plagues and Passover and the Red Sea and the Ten Commandments and the building of the tabernacle. It is a full book. Take it one chapter at a time.

You are on Day 2. You showed up again. That matters.

Heather

subject: Day 3: The one nobody looks forward to
body:
Good morning.

Leviticus. I know.

This is the book people quit on. All the rules about sacrifices and skin diseases and what to eat and what not to eat. It feels like reading a manual for a world that does not exist anymore.

But here is what I want you to see today. Every single rule in this book exists because God wanted to be close to His people. He was not trying to make their lives harder. He was teaching them how to live near a holy God and survive it.

The whole book is God saying, I want to dwell among you. Here is how.

So push through it. Read it fast if you need to. But do not skip it. There is something in there for you today.

If you are still going after Leviticus, you can handle anything this month throws at you.

Heather

subject: Day 4: Wandering starts here
body:
Good morning.

Numbers starts with a census. Then it turns into the story of a people who could not stop complaining.

God had rescued them. Parted the sea. Fed them from the sky. And they still grumbled. They still wanted to go back to Egypt. They still doubted.

And honestly, I see myself in them more than I want to admit.

How many times has God shown up in my life and I still doubted the next thing? How many times has He provided and I still worried about tomorrow?

That is the gift of reading the whole Bible like this. You start to see yourself in the story. Not always in the heroes. Sometimes in the people who could not stop looking back.

Keep going. You are almost through the wilderness.

Heather

subject: Day 5: Moses says goodbye
body:
Good morning.

It is Sunday.

You have read four books of the Bible this week. And woven through all of them is this idea of rest. In Genesis, God stopped on the seventh day. Not because He was tired. Because He was done, and what He made was good. In Exodus, He told the Israelites not to gather manna on the seventh day. He gave them a double portion on Friday so they would not have to work. Then He put rest right in the middle of the Ten Commandments. Remember the Sabbath. Keep it holy. In Leviticus, the rest went even further. Not just a day but a whole year every seven years. The land needed to breathe too.

Rest is not a reward for finishing your work. It is built into the rhythm God designed from the beginning.

Today is Deuteronomy, and Moses is going to repeat the commandments again. Including the Sabbath. But this time he gives a different reason. In Exodus, God said rest because He rested at creation. In Deuteronomy, Moses says rest because you were slaves in Egypt, and slaves do not get to rest. Rest is what free people do.

You are free. Rest in that today.

Deuteronomy is Moses giving his final speech. He knows he is not going into the Promised Land. He knows his time is almost up. And he spends his last days reminding the people of everything God has done.

Remember. Do not forget. Tell your children. Remember.

He says it over and over. Because he knows what happens when people forget.

Pay attention to the heart behind this book. This is a man who walked with God for forty years, standing at the edge of something he will never see, and his last words are not about himself. They are about making sure the next generation does not lose what matters.

Five days in. Five books down.

Heather

subject: Day 6: They finally get there
body:
Good morning.

After forty years in the wilderness, they cross into the Promised Land. Joshua is in charge now. And the very first thing God says to him is be strong and courageous.

He does not say be smart. He does not say have a plan. He says be strong and do not be afraid.

Joshua is full of battles and victories and territory being claimed. It moves fast. And there is something satisfying about reading it after all that wandering in Numbers and Deuteronomy.

They made it. Not because they were perfect. Because God kept His promise.

You are almost a week in. Be strong and keep going.

Heather

subject: Day 7: A boy in the temple hears God's voice
body:
Good morning.

Today is one of my favorite books. First Samuel. A woman named Hannah prays for a son. God gives her Samuel. She gives him back to God. And then this little boy lying in the temple hears the voice of God and does not even know what it is.

That image has always stayed with me. God speaking to a child in the dark. And the child saying, speak Lord, your servant is listening.

Then you get Saul. Then David. The giant. The friendship with Jonathan. The jealousy. The running. The caves.

First Samuel has everything. It reads like a novel. Enjoy it today.

Heather

subject: Day 8: David at his best and worst
body:
Good morning.

Second Samuel is David's reign. And it is complicated.

This is the man after God's own heart. The one who danced before the Lord. The one who wrote half the Psalms. And this is also the man who saw Bathsheba and everything fell apart.

I think we want our Bible heroes to stay heroes. But they do not. David is proof that you can love God deeply and still make devastating choices.

The thing that sets David apart is not that he never sinned. It is that he always came back. He repented. He grieved. He did not pretend.

That is the lesson I take from today. Not that I will get it right every time. But that when I do not, I can still come back.

Heather

subject: Day 9: Everything falls apart
body:
Good morning.

Second Kings is hard. You are watching two kingdoms fall. Bad king after bad king. A few good ones scattered in. Prophets warning. Nobody listening.

And then Babylon comes. Jerusalem falls. The temple that Solomon built gets destroyed. The people are carried into exile.

It is heavy. But do not rush past the grief of it. This matters. Because the rest of the Bible, the prophets, the Psalms, even the New Testament, is all shaped by this moment. Everything changed when the temple fell.

Some days the reading is going to be hard. Today is one of those days. But you are still here. And that matters.

Heather

subject: Day 10: The same story, different angle
body:
Good morning.

First Chronicles covers a lot of the same ground as Samuel and Kings. You are going to recognize stories. You might wonder why it is here.

Here is what I want you to notice. Chronicles was written after the exile. The people had lost everything and come back. And someone sat down and retold their history, but this time with an emphasis on worship. On the temple. On what God had done.

When you lose everything and then look back, you see different things. You see the hand of God in places you missed the first time.

Yes, the genealogies at the beginning are long. Power through them. The rest of the book will reward you.

Almost two weeks in. You are doing this.

Heather

subject: Day 11: They go home
body:
Good morning. Two weeks in.

Today is three books. Ezra, Nehemiah, and Esther. They are shorter and they move fast.

Ezra is about rebuilding the temple. Nehemiah is about rebuilding the wall. Esther is about a woman who saved her people by showing up when it mattered most.

All three books are about restoration. About going back to the rubble and building something again. About courage in hard places.

If you are feeling the weight of this challenge right now, if two weeks in feels like a lot, these three books are for you today. Because they are proof that broken things get rebuilt. And it starts with one person who says I will go.

You are halfway to halfway. Keep going.

Heather

subject: Day 12: The hardest question in the Bible
body:
Good morning.

Job. The whole thing. Forty-two chapters.

A man who did everything right loses everything. His children. His health. His wealth. His friends show up and tell him he must have done something wrong. He insists he did not. And for most of the book, God is silent.

And then God speaks. And He does not answer the question. He does not explain why. He just says, I am God and you are not. Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth?

That answer is not satisfying to our human brains. But it is the truth. We do not always get to know why. We just get to know who.

This book will wreck you if you let it. Let it.

You are almost halfway through the Bible.

Heather

subject: Day 13: God answers Job, and the songs begin
body:
Good morning.

Today you finish Job, and you get to the part everyone waits for. God finally speaks.

And here is what gets me every time. God never answers Job's question. He does not explain the suffering. Instead He asks Job about the ocean and the stars and the wild donkeys, and somehow that is enough. Job says, I had heard of you, but now my eyes have seen you.

Sometimes God does not give us answers. He gives us Himself. And it turns out that is what we actually needed.

Then, this very same day, you open the songbook. The Psalms. After twelve days of story and law and history, you get poetry. Real prayers from real people who were angry and afraid and grateful and amazed, sometimes all in the same chapter.

Do not rush the Psalms. Let a line stop you. When one does, that is not you falling behind. That is the whole point.

See you tomorrow.
Heather

subject: Day 14: Halfway. You made it to the Psalms.
body:
Good morning.

Sixteen days in. You are officially past the halfway mark of this challenge. And today you land in the Psalms.

The Psalms are different from everything you have read so far. This is not history. This is not law. This is people talking to God. Crying out. Praising. Asking why. Thanking Him. Begging for help. Declaring His faithfulness.

You are going to read fifty of them today. Some will hit you like a freight train. Some will feel repetitive. That is okay. The Psalms were never meant to be read in one sitting. But there is something about reading them in bulk that shows you the full range of what it looks like to walk with God.

Read them out loud if you can. Even a few. They were written to be spoken.

Halfway there. I am so proud of you.

Here is my one ask for the second half: tell someone.

Not so you have a buddy to keep you accountable. Tell them because of what this has been for you. If reading the Word this way has meant something, if it has shifted how you see God or how you read the Bible, there is someone in your life who needs that too. Good things are meant to be handed to other people.

You do not even have to find the words. Here is something you can copy, change to sound like you, and post or text to a friend:

"Reading the whole Bible in a month has changed how I read it. Not as individual verses and stories, but the big picture. I am halfway through. You can start any day you want. Come do it with me. heatherlynwilson.com/challenge #31DayBibleChallenge"

Post it, text it, drop it in your group chat. Someone else meeting God in His Word could start with your one sentence.

Heather

subject: Day 15: More Psalms. Stay with it.
body:
Good morning.

Fifty more Psalms today. And I want to point you to one in particular. Psalm 51.

This is David after Bathsheba. After the prophet Nathan confronted him. And David writes the most honest prayer of repentance in the entire Bible. Create in me a clean heart, O God.

That prayer has been prayed by millions of people over thousands of years. Because we have all been there. Maybe not David's sin. But the feeling of knowing you blew it and desperately needing God to make it right.

If you are behind on reading, this is your Psalm 51 moment. Do not quit. Just come back. Read today. That is enough.

Heather

subject: Day 16: The last of the Psalms
body:
Good morning.

Last fifty Psalms today. And they end with a crescendo.

Psalm 150. Let everything that has breath praise the Lord. That is how the book of Psalms closes. After all the crying, the questioning, the anger, the grief, the doubt, it ends with praise.

I think there is something in that for all of us. The journey does not end in the hard stuff. It ends in worship.

You just read the entire book of Psalms in three days. One hundred and fifty chapters. That is remarkable.

Eighteen days down. Thirteen to go.

Heather

subject: Day 17: Wisdom for the rest of your life
body:
Good morning.

Three books today. All wisdom literature. All different.

Proverbs is practical. Do this, not that. Fear the Lord, get wisdom, watch your mouth, work hard. You could read one chapter of Proverbs every day for a month and your life would change.

Ecclesiastes is the opposite. Solomon, the wisest man alive, looking at everything and saying it is all meaningless. It sounds depressing until you realize what he is actually saying. Without God, none of it matters. That is not despair. That is the most honest thing anyone has ever written.

Song of Solomon is a love poem. It is in the Bible and it is beautiful and it is supposed to be there.

Enjoy today. After the weight of Job and Psalms, this is a different kind of reading.

Heather

subject: Day 18: The prophet nobody wanted to listen to
body:
Good morning.

You are in the prophets now. And we start with Isaiah, the biggest of them all.

Isaiah is two things at once. It is God saying to His people, you have wandered so far and judgment is coming. And it is God saying, but I am not done with you. A savior is coming. Comfort my people.

Today is the first half. The harder half. Judgment. Warnings. Consequences. But even in the middle of it, you will find verses that stop you in your tracks. For unto us a child is born. That is Isaiah 9.

The prophets are harder to read than the stories. They are poetry and proclamation mixed together. Do not worry about understanding every verse. Just keep moving forward.

Twenty days. You are almost there.

Heather

subject: Day 19: Comfort, comfort my people
body:
Good morning. Three weeks in.

Today is the second half of Isaiah. And the tone changes. Starting around chapter 40, you hit some of the most beautiful passages in the Bible.

Comfort, comfort my people. Those who wait on the Lord shall renew their strength. He was wounded for our transgressions. By his stripes we are healed.

Isaiah wrote these words hundreds of years before Jesus. And when you read them now, knowing the rest of the story, it takes your breath away.

This might be your favorite day of reading this entire month. Let it soak in.

Three weeks done. Ten days left. You are going to finish this.

Heather

subject: Day 20: The prophet who did not want the job
body:
Good morning.

Jeremiah was called before he was born. And his first response was, I am too young. I do not know how to speak.

Sound familiar? Moses said the same thing. Gideon said the same thing. Every person God calls seems to start by explaining why they are the wrong choice.

Jeremiah spent his entire life preaching to people who would not listen. He wept over a nation that refused to turn back. He was thrown in prison. Dropped in a muddy cistern. And he kept going.

Sometimes faithfulness does not look like success. Sometimes it just looks like showing up to the thing God asked you to do, even when nobody is responding.

Nine days left. Keep showing up.

Heather

subject: Day 21: Jerusalem falls. Jeremiah weeps.
body:
Good morning.

Today you finish Jeremiah and read Lamentations. And it is heavy.

Jerusalem falls. The thing Jeremiah warned about for decades finally happens. And then Lamentations is his grief poured out on the page. Five chapters of mourning.

But right in the middle, chapter 3, you will find this. Great is His faithfulness. His mercies are new every morning.

That verse was not written on a good day. It was written in the ruins. And that is what makes it so powerful. It is not optimism. It is faith that survived the worst thing.

If you are tired today, if this challenge feels like a lot, read Lamentations 3:22-23. Mercy is new this morning. For you too.

Heather

subject: Day 22: Visions, bones, and a valley that comes alive
body:
Good morning.

Big day today. Ezekiel and Daniel.

Ezekiel is strange and beautiful. Wheels within wheels. A valley of dry bones that come back to life. A temple described in painstaking detail. This is a prophet who saw things no one else saw.

The valley of dry bones in chapter 37 is one of the most powerful images in all of Scripture. Can these bones live? And God says, watch me.

Daniel is the lion's den. The fiery furnace. Three young men who said, our God is able to deliver us, but even if He does not, we will not bow.

Even if He does not. That is the kind of faith I want.

One week left. Seven more days.

Heather

subject: Day 23: Twelve books in one day
reading: Hosea 5–14, Joel 1–3, Amos 1–9, Obadiah, Jonah 1–4, Micah 1–7, Nahum 1–3, Habakkuk 1–3
body:
Good morning.

Today is the minor prophets. All twelve of them. They are called minor because they are short, not because they are less important.

Hosea is about a prophet told to marry an unfaithful woman as a picture of God's love for Israel. Joel is about a plague of locusts and the day of the Lord. Amos is a shepherd who told the rich to stop exploiting the poor. Jonah ran from God and ended up in a fish.

Micah tells you what God requires. Do justice. Love mercy. Walk humbly.

Habakkuk asks God why bad things happen and gets an answer he did not expect.

Malachi is the last word of the Old Testament. And then silence. Four hundred years of silence before the New Testament begins.

You just finished the Old Testament. Let that sink in. Tomorrow you open to Matthew.

Heather

subject: Day 24: Jesus is here
body:
Good morning.

After everything you have read, all the promises and prophecies and waiting, today you open to the New Testament. And the very first word of Matthew connects Jesus to Abraham and David. The whole story has been leading here.

Two Gospels today. Matthew and Mark. Matthew is detailed and teaching-heavy. The Sermon on the Mount is in chapters 5 through 7 and it will change your life if you let it. Mark is fast. He uses the word immediately more than any other writer. Everything moves.

You have spent 25 days reading about a God who promised He would come. Today He arrives.

Six days left.

Heather

subject: Day 25: The cross, the empty tomb, and a manger
body:
Good morning.

Today is a big one. You will read the crucifixion and the resurrection in Matthew, then all of Mark, and then, of all things, you will end the day at the manger in Luke.

Strange order? Maybe. But think about what it does. You will watch Jesus die and rise, hear Mark tell the whole story again at full speed, and then see the baby in the feed trough and know exactly who He is and exactly what He came to do.

Mark is my favorite gospel to read fast. His favorite word is immediately. Jesus moves through Mark like a man on a mission, because He was.

By tonight you will have seen the whole gospel story twice and its beginning a third time. Let it stack up in you. This is the center of everything we believe.

See you tomorrow.
Heather

subject: Day 26: Two more portraits of Jesus
body:
Good morning.

Luke and John today. Two more Gospels. Same Jesus. Completely different angles.

Luke is the historian. He tells you about the shepherds, the prodigal son, the good Samaritan, Zacchaeus in the tree. He notices the people everyone else overlooks. The poor. The women. The outsiders.

John is the poet. In the beginning was the Word. I am the bread of life. I am the light of the world. I am the resurrection and the life. John is not trying to give you facts. He is trying to show you who Jesus really is.

You have now read all four Gospels. Four witnesses. One story. And you are four days from the finish line.

Heather

subject: Day 27: Believe, and then go
body:
Good morning.

Today you finish John and watch the church be born in Acts.

John wrote his gospel for one reason, and he tells you what it is near the end. These are written so that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that by believing you may have life in his name. Every sign, every conversation, every I AM statement is aimed at that one target. Your belief.

And then Acts. The same disciples who hid behind locked doors are suddenly standing in the streets preaching to thousands. What changed? They saw Him alive, and then the Holy Spirit showed up. The church does not grow in Acts because the plan was clever. It grows because God was in it.

That same Spirit is in you. That is not a nice thought. It is the actual claim of this book.

See you tomorrow.
Heather

subject: Day 28: The church explodes and Paul changes everything
body:
Good morning.

Acts is one of the most exciting books in the Bible. Jesus ascends. The Holy Spirit falls. Peter preaches and 3,000 people believe in a single day. And then a man named Saul, who was killing Christians, gets knocked off his horse and becomes Paul, the greatest missionary who ever lived.

The book of Acts reads like an action movie. Shipwrecks. Prison breaks. Miracles. Riots. And through all of it, the gospel spreads.

Then Romans. Paul's masterpiece. This is the deepest theology in the New Testament. For all have sinned. Nothing can separate us from the love of God. Take it slow if you can. Romans is dense but every sentence matters.

Three more days.

P.S. I do not want you to lose this momentum when you finish. Whenever you are ready for what is next, One Book Deep is open: the book of James every day for a month, going deep instead of fast. heatherlynwilson.com/challenge-james


Heather

subject: Day 29: Letters to churches that sound like they were written yesterday
reading: 1 Corinthians 8–16, 2 Corinthians 1–13, Galatians 1–6, Ephesians 1–6, Philippians 1–4, Colossians 1–2
body:
Good morning.

Paul's letters today. And they are surprisingly practical.

Corinthians is Paul writing to a messy church. Divisions. Lawsuits. Arguments about food. And right in the middle, chapter 13, the love chapter. Love is patient. Love is kind. You have heard it at weddings. But Paul did not write it for weddings. He wrote it for a church that was tearing itself apart.

Galatians is freedom. Ephesians is identity. Philippians is joy written from a prison cell. Colossians is who Jesus really is.

These letters are short. They read fast. And they will hit you differently after having read the whole Old Testament to get here. You understand now what they are building on.

Two more days.

P.S. Two days left. Start thinking about what comes next. One Book Deep is open, the book of James every day for a month: heatherlynwilson.com/challenge-james. Or see every challenge that is open at heatherlynwilson.com/challenge


Heather

subject: Day 30: One more day after this
reading: Colossians 3–4, 1 Thessalonians 1–5, 2 Thessalonians 1–3, 1 Timothy 1–6, 2 Timothy 1–4, Titus 1–3, Philemon, Hebrews 1–13, James 1–3
body:
Good morning.

Penultimate day. You are one day away from finishing.

Today is the rest of Paul's letters plus Hebrews. These are shorter books. Some are only a few chapters. But they are full.

Thessalonians is about the return of Jesus. Timothy and Titus are Paul coaching younger leaders. Philemon is a one-page letter about a runaway slave that will break your heart.

And then Hebrews. Nobody knows for sure who wrote it. But it ties the entire Old Testament to Jesus in a way that will make everything you have read this month click into place. Chapter 11 is the faith hall of fame. By faith Abraham. By faith Moses. By faith Rahab. These are your people now. You have read their stories.

One more day. You are going to finish this.

P.S. Tomorrow is your last day. It does not have to be the end. One Book Deep, the book of James every day for a month, is open whenever you are ready: heatherlynwilson.com/challenge-james


Heather

subject: Day 31: You did it.
reading: James 4–5, 1 Peter 1–5, 2 Peter 1–3, 1 John 1–5, 2 John, 3 John, Jude, Revelation 1–22
body:
Good morning.

This is it. Day 31. The last day.

James is practical faith. Do not just hear the word, do it. First Peter is hope in suffering. Second Peter is holding on. John's letters are about love. Jude is a warning. And then Revelation.

Revelation is wild and beautiful and confusing and hopeful all at once. Do not try to figure out every symbol. Just read it and let the ending wash over you. Because the Bible ends with a promise. He is making all things new. There will be no more tears. No more death. No more pain.

The story that started in a garden ends in a city. The story that started with God walking with two people ends with God dwelling among all His people forever.

You just read the entire Bible in 31 days.

I do not know what this month has done in your heart. But I know God's Word does not return empty. Something shifted. Something grew. Something was planted that will keep growing long after today.

I am so proud of you. Thank you for reading alongside me.

P.S. And I am not done. Each time you read the Word, God can show you new things about Himself and about yourself. Whenever you are ready for the next step: One Book Deep, the book of James every day for a month, at heatherlynwilson.com/challenge-james. Or see everything that is open at heatherlynwilson.com/challenge
